key_insight: ShipNet uses geometric deep learning on hull point clouds to rapidly predict both local pressure and far-field wave patterns from ship geometry and speed.
engineering_relevance: It enables near-real-time hydrodynamic screening for ship design, supporting faster parametric exploration than traditional CFD.
method: Regularized dynamic graph convolutional backbone on hull point clouds
Multi-head decoder for hull-surface pressure and free-surface elevation
Composite loss combining point-wise regression and image-structure terms
evidence_signal: Trained on 420 inviscid potential-flow simulations from two parent yacht hulls, ShipNet reached R^2=0.98 for pressure and R^2=0.91 for wave fields, with about 0.15 s inference time per case.
watch_item: Performance is limited to the studied hull families, speed range, and inviscid training data, so generalization to broader, viscous flows remains unproven.
paper_title: ShipNet: A Geometric Deep Learning Surrogate for Real-Time Ship Hydrodynamics
